scope: Current product source; source-built four-ABI Android AAR and macOS arm64 Kotlin JAR, each installed into a fresh consumer. Android execution is limited to an owned API 35 arm64-v8a emulator; the other three packaged ABIs are build-only.
toolchains: Rust 1.96.0, Temurin 17.0.19+10, Gradle 8.14.6, Kotlin 2.2.21, AGP 8.13.2, Android SDK 35, NDK 27.3.13750724, emulator 37.2.12, Google APIs arm64-v8a API 35 image revision 9. Existing Cargo locks must remain unchanged.
buildFix: The iOS clean-build failure already reproduced rust-lang/rust#157750 with symbol and debuginfo stripping. Kotlin macOS host builds now default to no stripping; Android builds disable stripping only for host build dependencies via the documented Cargo build-override. No global security settings change.
checks: All seven existing JVM tests through the extracted JAR. All seven existing JVM lifecycle tests adapted only for Android JUnit annotations and an app-private temporary directory, plus both existing Android instrumented tests through the extracted AAR: nine normal Android tests with no skips. Build/install/launch the existing Compose sample and verify its store directory exists. Verify every native archive member against its compiled library.
recovery: Two owned emulator cases, plaintext and encrypted: insert 32 documents, replace 16 and delete eight; after each phase complete a public snapshot, which compacts and flushes the live store. A private acknowledgement file is fsynced by the writer, then validated and fsynced into the host ledger before am force-stop kills that consumer. A new process verifies all 24 survivors, all eight deletions, replacement text/metadata and a subsequent write/snapshot/reopen. This qualifies only the completed-snapshot boundary, not arbitrary interruption or device power loss.
archiveVerification: V1 rejected expected Gradle stripping. V2 independently reproduced NDK llvm-strip --strip-unneeded for all four libraries with byte-identical AAR and Gradle output. Retain compiled and packaged hashes and require this exact transformation in subsequent versions.
androidLockRegression: V2 executed all nine lifecycle cases; eight failed opening a store because Rust 1.96 File::try_lock excludes Android. V3 uses the existing libc flock on Android, preserving std behavior elsewhere, in the shared file helper used by store, vector-update and experimental graph ownership. Run 10 focused native lock/path checks inside the owned Android emulator, including native-flock interoperability, cloned-descriptor lifetime, hardlink/symlink/FIFO rejection and both graph ownership paths. Rebuild every library and rerun all lifecycle/recovery checks; reuse no pre-fix package.
resources: Local/free; start after the owner-membership timing screen ends. Dedicated source/work/consumer/AVD directories; at most two build workers and emulator cores. Never touch the Intel soak, other emulators, held-out inputs, credentials or global security controls. Retain failures and raw receipts.
limits: Physical devices, other Android releases/ABIs, legacy migration and other host platforms remain open. These results establish no latency advantage or independent reproduction.
